stem.en: A Bryophyllum leaf falls on damp soil, and tiny plantlets grow along its edge. Where do the new plants come from?

text.en: Pollen that reached the leaf from another plant

feedback.en: Pollen is not involved. No flower or second plant is needed here.

text.en: Seeds that were hidden along the edge of the leaf

feedback.en: A leaf holds no seeds. The plantlets are not grown from seed.

text.en: Roots of the parent that grew up into the leaf

feedback.en: Roots do not grow up into a leaf. Each plantlet forms its own small roots.

text.en: The leaf itself, a growing part of the plant

feedback.en: Yes. This is vegetative propagation: a new plant from a growing part.

explanation.en: The plantlets sprout from the leaf, a growing part of the plant. No seed and no second parent are involved, so this is vegetative propagation.

hints.en: Is a seed or a second plant needed here?
A leaf is one of the growing parts of a plant.
